topics: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the charge on one electron?
questions.explanation: The elementary charge is e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C; 9.1 × 10^-31 is the electron's mass in kg.

questions.q: Quantisation of electric charge means that
options: a body can carry any fractional amount of the charge e
the charge on a body is always an integral multiple of e
the charge on a body is always an even multiple of e
charge can be created on one body without an equal opposite charge elsewhere
questions.explanation: Charge exists in discrete packets, so q = ne where n is an integer.

questions.q: Two point charges of 3 μC each are placed 30 cm apart in air. Taking k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C², the force between them is
If the distance between two point charges is doubled while the charges stay the same, the electrostatic force between them becomes
questions.explanation: By Coulomb's law F is proportional to 1/r², so doubling r makes F one-fourth.

questions.q: Two identical small conducting spheres carry +6 μC and -2 μC. They are touched together and then returned to their original separation. The magnitude of the force after contact compared with the magnitude before contact is
questions.explanation: Before: product = 12 (in μC²). After sharing, each has +2 μC so product = 4. Ratio of forces = 4/12 = 1/3.

questions.q: A point charge q is placed at the centre of a cube. Assuming the cube is a closed surface, the electric flux through any one face is
questions.explanation: Total flux q/ε0 by Gauss's law is shared equally among six identical faces, giving q/(6ε0) each.

questions.q: Find the magnitude and direction of the electric field at a distance of 2 m from a point charge of +4 μC in air (k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²).
questions.answer: E = 9 × 10^3 N/C, directed radially away from the charge.
keyPoints: Direction is away from a positive charge
questions.explanation: Substituting into E = kq/r² gives 9000 N/C; the field of a positive charge points outward.

questions.q: Why can two electric field lines never cross each other?
questions.answer: At the point of intersection there would be two tangents, meaning two different directions of the electric field at one point, but the field at any point has a single, definite direction.
keyPoints: Tangent to a field line gives the field direction
Crossing would give two directions at one point
The field at a point is unique
questions.explanation: A unique field direction at each point forbids intersection of field lines.

questions.q: One volt is equal to
questions.explanation: Potential is work done per unit charge, so 1 V = 1 J/C.

questions.q: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor increases when
options: the area of the plates is increased
the distance between the plates is increased
the potential difference across it is doubled
the charge on the plates is halved
questions.explanation: C = ε0A/d depends only on geometry and medium; larger area gives larger C.

questions.q: Two capacitors of 4 μF and 12 μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is
The energy stored in a 10 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is
A parallel plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab is now inserted between the plates. The energy stored in the capacitor
questions.explanation: Charge Q stays constant while C increases, and U = Q²/2C, so U decreases.

questions.q: Two equal and opposite point charges are placed some distance apart. At the midpoint of the line joining them
options: both the potential and the field are zero
the potential is non-zero and the field is zero
both the potential and the field are non-zero
the potential is zero and the field is non-zero
questions.explanation: The potentials of +q and -q cancel, but the two fields point the same way and add.

questions.q: Calculate the electric potential at a distance of 3 cm from a point charge of 2 nC in air (k = 9 × 10^9 N m²/C²).
questions.explanation: kq = 18 V·m, and dividing by 0.03 m gives 600 V.

questions.q: A 5 μF parallel plate capacitor stays connected to a 12 V battery while the separation between its plates is doubled. Find the new charge on it and the new stored energy.
questions.answer: New charge = 30 μC; new energy = 1.8 × 10^-4 J (180 μJ).
keyPoints: Doubling d halves C to 2.5 μF
V stays 12 V, so Q = CV = 2.5 × 12 = 30 μC
questions.explanation: With the battery connected V is fixed, so both Q and U are halved from their original values of 60 μC and 360 μJ.

questions.q: The SI unit of resistivity is
questions.explanation: From R = ρl/A, ρ = RA/l has unit ohm × m² / m = ohm-metre.

questions.q: The drift velocity of electrons in a conductor is
options: the speed of electrons between collisions at room temperature
the speed with which the electric signal travels along the wire
the speed of the electromagnetic wave in the wire
the average velocity gained by free electrons due to the applied electric field
questions.explanation: Drift velocity is the small net average velocity superimposed on random thermal motion by the field.

questions.q: A wire of resistance 10 Ω is uniformly stretched to double its length without change in volume. Its new resistance is
questions.explanation: Length doubles and area halves, so R = ρl/A becomes four times: 40 Ω.

questions.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to an external resistance of 5 Ω. The terminal voltage is
questions.explanation: I = 12/(5 + 1) = 2 A, so terminal voltage V = IR = 2 × 5 = 10 V.

questions.q: Two bulbs rated 60 W and 100 W at 220 V are connected in series across 220 V. Which statement is correct?
options: The 100 W bulb glows brighter because its power rating is higher
Both glow equally because the current is the same
Neither glows because the voltage is shared
The 60 W bulb glows brighter because it has the larger resistance and carries the same current
questions.explanation: R = V²/P so the 60 W bulb has more resistance; in series P = I²R is larger for it.

questions.q: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, P = 10 Ω and Q = 20 Ω lie in one arm pair and R = 15 Ω and an unknown S lie in the other, with P/Q = R/S. The value of S is
An electric bulb is marked 60 W, 240 V. Find the current it draws and its resistance when working normally.
questions.explanation: Power rating gives the current directly, and Ohm's law then gives the resistance.

questions.q: A copper wire of cross-section 1 mm² carries a current of 2 A. If the free electron density is 8.5 × 10^28 m^-3 and e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C, find the drift speed of electrons.
questions.explanation: The drift speed is a fraction of a millimetre per second, far smaller than thermal speeds.

questions.q: A charged particle moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force on it is
options: such that it moves in a circle
questions.explanation: F = qvB sinθ and θ = 0° for parallel motion, so F = 0.

questions.q: The work done by a magnetic force on a moving charged particle is always
questions.explanation: The magnetic force is perpendicular to velocity, so it does no work and the speed stays constant.

questions.q: A proton moves at 2 × 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. The magnetic force on it is (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C)
The magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop of radius 10 cm carrying a current of 5 A is (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A)
An electron moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field. If its speed is doubled (field unchanged), the time period of revolution
questions.explanation: T = 2πm/(qB) does not depend on speed; the radius doubles but so does the path length covered per unit time.

questions.q: Two long parallel wires, 0.1 m apart, each carry 10 A in the same direction. The force per unit length between them is (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A)
questions.explanation: F/L = μ0I1I2/(2πd) = 2 × 10^-7 × 100/0.1 = 2 × 10^-4 N/m; parallel currents attract.

questions.q: A straight conductor 0.5 m long carries 4 A at right angles to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. Find the force on it.
questions.explanation: At right angles sinθ = 1, so F = BIL = 0.4 N.

questions.q: Find the cyclotron frequency of a proton in a magnetic field of 1.0 T (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C, mass of proton = 1.67 × 10^-27 kg).
questions.explanation: The frequency depends only on q, m and B, not on the proton's speed.

questions.q: Which statement about magnetic field lines is correct?
options: They start at the north pole and end at the south pole of the magnet only
They start from isolated magnetic monopoles
questions.explanation: Since isolated monopoles do not exist, field lines continue inside the magnet and form closed loops.

questions.q: Substances that are weakly repelled by a magnetic field are called
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials have negative susceptibility and move away from stronger field regions.

questions.q: A magnetic dipole of moment 2 A m² is placed in a uniform field of 0.5 T at 30° to the field. The torque on it is
questions.explanation: τ = MB sinθ = 2 × 0.5 × sin30° = 0.5 N m.

questions.q: Above the Curie temperature a ferromagnetic material behaves as a
questions.explanation: Thermal agitation destroys domain alignment, so the material becomes paramagnetic.

questions.q: Soft iron is chosen for the core of an electromagnet because it has
questions.explanation: High permeability gives strong magnetisation and low retentivity lets it demagnetise easily when current stops.

questions.q: The core of a transformer, which is magnetised and demagnetised many times per second, should have a hysteresis loop that is
options: tall and wide with large area
questions.explanation: Loop area equals the energy lost as heat per cycle, so a narrow loop minimises loss.

questions.q: Define magnetic declination and angle of dip at a place.
questions.answer: Declination is the angle between the geographic meridian and the magnetic meridian at the place. Dip is the angle that the Earth's total magnetic field makes with the horizontal at the place.
keyPoints: Declination: angle between geographic and magnetic meridians
Dip: angle of total field with the horizontal
questions.explanation: Together with the horizontal component they describe the Earth's magnetic field at a place.

questions.q: A material has magnetic susceptibility 2999. Find its relative permeability and the magnetic field B inside it when H = 100 A/m (μ0 = 4π × 10^-7 T m/A).
questions.explanation: Relative permeability is 1 plus susceptibility, and B = μ0μrH.

questions.q: According to Faraday's law, the induced emf in a coil is proportional to the
options: rate of change of magnetic flux linked with it
questions.explanation: emf = -N dΦ/dt, so it depends on how fast the flux changes.

questions.q: Lenz's law is a consequence of the law of conservation of
questions.explanation: The induced current opposes the change causing it, otherwise energy would be created from nothing.

questions.q: The magnetic flux through a coil of 100 turns changes from 0.04 Wb to 0.01 Wb in 0.1 s. The magnitude of the induced emf is
A metal rod 0.5 m long moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T, with its length perpendicular to both. The motional emf across its ends is
A strong magnet dropped through a long vertical copper tube falls much more slowly than through air. This is because
options: eddy currents induced in the tube oppose the magnet's motion
copper is a magnetic material that attracts the magnet
air resistance inside the tube is large
the magnet loses its magnetism inside copper
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law, induced eddy currents produce a magnetic force opposing the fall.

questions.q: A long solenoid's number of turns is doubled while its length and cross-sectional area stay the same. Its self-inductance becomes
questions.explanation: L = μ0N²A/l is proportional to N², so doubling N gives four times L.

questions.q: The current in a 2 H inductor changes from 3 A to 1 A in 0.5 s. Find the magnitude of the induced emf.
questions.explanation: Back emf is the inductance times the rate of change of current.

questions.q: Find the energy stored in a 0.5 H inductor carrying 4 A. By what factor does the energy change if the current is doubled?
questions.answer: Energy = 4 J; it becomes four times (16 J) when the current is doubled.
questions.explanation: Magnetic energy varies as the square of the current.

questions.q: The rms value of an alternating voltage of peak value V0 is
In an AC circuit containing only a resistor, the phase difference between voltage and current is
questions.explanation: For a pure resistor, voltage and current are in phase.

questions.q: An inductor of 0.1/π H is connected to a 50 Hz AC source. Its inductive reactance is
A capacitor of (100/π) μF is connected to a 50 Hz AC source. Its capacitive reactance is
A series LCR circuit has L = 0.1 H and C = 10 μF. Its resonant angular frequency is
An ideal step-down transformer converts 2200 V to 220 V and the secondary delivers 5 A. The primary current is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs, so Ip = 220 × 5/2200 = 0.5 A.

questions.q: A resistance of 30 Ω is in series with an inductive reactance of 40 Ω in an AC circuit. Find the impedance and the power factor.
questions.explanation: The power factor is the ratio of resistance to impedance.

questions.q: An alternating voltage is given by v = 100√2 sin(100πt) volts. Find its rms value and frequency.
keyPoints: Peak V0 = 100√2 V so Vrms = V0/√2 = 100 V
questions.explanation: Comparing with v = V0 sin ωt gives V0 and ω directly.

questions.q: The speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum is approximately
questions.explanation: All electromagnetic waves travel at c ≈ 3 × 10^8 m/s in vacuum.

questions.q: Which of the following electromagnetic radiations has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Radio waves lie at the low-frequency, long-wavelength end of the spectrum.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave in vacuum has wavelength 3 m. Its frequency is
Displacement current exists in a region where
options: the electric flux changes with time
charges flow physically through a wire
questions.explanation: Maxwell's displacement current is ε0 dΦ_E/dt, produced by a time-varying electric field.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travels along the +x direction with its electric field along +y. The magnetic field is along
questions.explanation: E × B must point along the propagation direction: ŷ × ẑ = x̂, so B is along +z.

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves are not deflected by electric or magnetic fields because they
options: travel at a very high speed
questions.explanation: Deflection requires force on charge, and the waves themselves are uncharged.

questions.q: An FM radio station transmits at 100 MHz. Find the wavelength of the wave in air (c = 3 × 10^8 m/s).
questions.explanation: Wavelength is speed divided by frequency.

questions.q: Explain how Maxwell's displacement current removes the inconsistency in Ampère's circuital law for a capacitor that is being charged.
questions.answer: Between the plates there is no conduction current, so Ampère's law applied to a surface passing between the plates would give zero while a surface cutting the wire gives a non-zero value. A changing electric field between the plates gives a displacement current equal to the conduction current in the wire, making the results agree.
keyPoints: No conduction current flows between the plates
Two surfaces bounded by the same loop gave different answers
Displacement current ε0 dΦ_E/dt equals the conduction current
questions.explanation: Adding the displacement current term makes the total current continuous.

questions.q: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from
options: a denser to a rarer medium at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle
a rarer to a denser medium at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle
a denser to a rarer medium at an angle of incidence less than the critical angle
any medium to another at normal incidence
questions.explanation: Both conditions are needed: denser to rarer and angle beyond the critical angle.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. Its radius of curvature is
questions.explanation: R = 2f = 30 cm.

questions.q: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 20 cm in front of it. The image is
options: 40 cm in front of the mirror
20 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: Using 1/v + 1/u = 1/f with u = -20, f = -10 gives v = -20 cm, a real image at the centre of curvature.

questions.q: The power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm is
An object is placed 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. The image distance and magnification are
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60 so v = 60 cm and m = v/u = 60/(-30) = -2 (real, inverted, enlarged).

questions.q: A prism of angle 60° has refractive index √2. The angle of minimum deviation is
A swimming pool has real depth 2.4 m of water (refractive index 4/3). Find the apparent depth when viewed from directly above.
questions.explanation: For near-normal viewing, the bottom appears raised by a factor 1/n.

questions.q: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +20 cm and -30 cm are placed in contact. Find the combined focal length and power, and say whether the combination is converging or diverging.
questions.answer: Combined focal length = +60 cm, power ≈ +1.67 D, converging.
questions.explanation: Powers add for thin lenses in contact: +5 D - 3.33 D = +1.67 D.

questions.q: The wavefront from a point source in a uniform medium is
questions.explanation: Points equidistant from a point source lie on a sphere.

questions.q: Which phenomenon shows that light waves are transverse?
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarised.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, λ = 600 nm, slit separation 0.5 mm and screen distance 1 m. The fringe width is
In single slit diffraction, if the slit width is decreased, the central maximum becomes
questions.explanation: The angular width of the central maximum is 2λ/a, which increases as a decreases.

questions.q: Unpolarised light of intensity I0 passes through a polariser and then through an analyser whose axis makes 60° with the polariser. The final intensity is
questions.explanation: After the polariser I0/2; by Malus's law, (I0/2)cos²60° = (I0/2)(1/4) = I0/8.

questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, a point on the screen where the path difference is 1.5λ is
options: a point of half the maximum intensity
questions.explanation: A path difference of an odd multiple of λ/2 (here 3λ/2) gives destructive interference.

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment in air the fringe width is 0.8 mm. What would it be if the whole apparatus is immersed in water of refractive index 4/3?
keyPoints: Fringe width is proportional to λ
questions.explanation: Immersion in a medium of index n reduces the fringe width by the factor n.

questions.q: Find the polarising (Brewster) angle for glass of refractive index √3. What is the angle between the reflected and refracted rays at this angle?
questions.answer: Brewster angle = 60°; the reflected and refracted rays are at 90° to each other.
keyPoints: Angle between reflected and refracted rays = 180° - 60° - 30° = 90°
questions.explanation: At Brewster's angle i_B + r = 90°, so the rays are perpendicular.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: The photoelectric effect supports the
questions.explanation: Einstein explained it by treating light as photons, each carrying energy hf.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: The threshold frequency of a metal is the
options: minimum frequency of light below which no photoelectrons are emitted
maximum frequency of light that can be absorbed
frequency at which electrons emit most quickly
frequency at which the stopping potential is zero for all metals
questions.explanation: Below the threshold frequency the photon energy is less than the work function, so no emission occurs.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Taking hc = 1240 eV nm, the energy of a photon of wavelength 400 nm is

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: A metal has work function 2 eV. Light of photon energy 5 eV falls on it. The stopping potential is
questions.explanation: K_max = 5 - 2 = 3 eV, so V0 = 3 V.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: An electron is accelerated from rest through 150 V. Its de Broglie wavelength is closest to (h = 6.63 × 10^-34 J s, m = 9.1 × 10^-31 kg, e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C)

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Monochromatic light of fixed frequency above threshold falls on a photocell. If the intensity of the light is doubled, then
options: both the saturation current and the stopping potential double
the stopping potential doubles and the saturation current is unchanged
neither the saturation current nor the stopping potential changes
the saturation current doubles while the stopping potential is unchanged
questions.explanation: More photons per second means more electrons per second, but each photon's energy, hence the stopping potential, is unchanged.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.1 kg ball moving at 10 m/s (h = 6.63 × 10^-34 J s). Why is its wave nature not observed?
questions.answer: λ = 6.63 × 10^-34 m, far too small to detect.
keyPoints: Much smaller than any size we can measure, so no diffraction is seen
questions.explanation: Wave effects appear only when λ is comparable to the sizes involved.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.q: Light of wavelength 300 nm falls on a metal of work function 2.3 eV. Find the stopping potential (hc = 1240 eV nm).
questions.explanation: eV0 = hf - φ.

questions.q: Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment showed that
options: electrons are embedded in a uniformly positive sphere
most of the atom's mass and positive charge is concentrated in a tiny nucleus
questions.explanation: Large-angle scattering of a few alpha particles indicated a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have
options: the same mass number but different atomic numbers
the same atomic number but different mass numbers
questions.explanation: Isotopes share Z but differ in neutron number, hence in A.

questions.q: In the Bohr model of hydrogen, the energy of the n = 2 level is
A radioactive sample has a half-life of 20 days. The fraction of the sample left after 60 days is
questions.explanation: 60 days is three half-lives, so the fraction is (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.q: A hydrogen atom drops from n = 3 to n = 2. Taking hc = 1240 eV nm and E_n = -13.6/n² eV, the wavelength of the emitted photon is closest to
Fusion of two light nuclei releases energy mainly because
options: the binding energy per nucleon of the product is lower than that of the reactants
the binding energy per nucleon of the product is higher than that of the reactants
nucleons are destroyed in the process
questions.explanation: Moving up the binding-energy curve means a more tightly bound nucleus, and the mass defect is released as energy.

questions.q: A nuclear reaction has a mass defect of 0.03 u. Find the energy released in MeV (1 u = 931.5 MeV/c²).
questions.explanation: Mass defect multiplied by the energy equivalent of 1 u.

questions.q: A radioactive source has a half-life of 10 hours and an initial activity of 800 Bq. What is its activity after 30 hours?
questions.explanation: Activity decays exponentially just as the number of nuclei does.

questions.q: An n-type semiconductor is made by doping pure silicon with
options: a pentavalent impurity such as phosphorus
a trivalent impurity such as boron
a tetravalent impurity such as carbon
questions.explanation: Pentavalent atoms donate an extra electron, so electrons are the majority carriers.

questions.q: When a p-n junction is forward biased, the depletion layer
questions.explanation: The applied field opposes the barrier potential, reducing the width of the depletion region.

questions.q: A full-wave rectifier is fed with a 50 Hz AC input. The frequency of the pulsating output is
questions.explanation: Both half cycles are rectified, so the output ripple frequency is twice the input frequency.

questions.q: In which type of solid do the conduction band and valence band overlap?
questions.explanation: Overlapping bands let metals conduct freely with no energy gap to cross.

questions.q: A Zener diode is used as a voltage regulator when it operates in
options: reverse bias below the breakdown voltage
questions.explanation: In breakdown the voltage across a Zener stays almost constant over a wide range of current.

questions.q: A NAND gate has its two inputs connected together. The resulting circuit behaves as a
questions.explanation: With A = B, NAND gives (A·A)' = A', which is NOT.

questions.q: Write the truth table of a two-input OR gate.
questions.answer: Inputs (A, B) and output Y: (0,0) gives 0; (0,1) gives 1; (1,0) gives 1; (1,1) gives 1.
keyPoints: Output is 1 if at least one input is 1
Output is 0 only when both inputs are 0
questions.explanation: OR gives a high output whenever any input is high.

questions.q: Explain why the resistivity of a semiconductor decreases with temperature while that of a metal increases.
questions.answer: In a semiconductor heating breaks more covalent bonds, creating many more electron-hole pairs, so carrier density rises greatly and outweighs the extra collisions. In a metal the carrier density is almost fixed and heating increases lattice vibrations and collisions, reducing the relaxation time.
keyPoints: Semiconductor: carrier density rises strongly with temperature
Metal: more collisions, shorter relaxation time, higher resistivity
questions.explanation: Which effect dominates, carrier number or collision rate, decides the sign of the temperature coefficient.
